system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (T4C), fallback target.**

- **Customer convenience right (§3.4, p0044–p0045):** we may terminate the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for convenience on at least one month's notice, effective at month-end — better than the 60–90 day fallback, so already met.
- **Vendor side (§3.3, §3.2):** IBM has no mid-term convenience exit; its only routes are material breach or non-renewal at the end of a term on 90 days' notice, which satisfies both Vendor-side fallback elements. Non-renewal is left to RENEWAL and not double-flagged.
- **Material gap (§3.4(b), p0046):** our convenience right is conditioned on uncapped "early termination charges" in Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments. One surgical insertion adds the fallback cap ("capped at three (3) months' charges") with all other wording preserved.
- Preferred pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is noted in the rationale only, not flagged.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Deterministic failures:
- Customer convenience termination present: failed

Verifier reasons:
- Position-complete at the fallback: all four fallback elements are met after the edit, so the redline is sufficient as drafted. Preferred is not reached (no pro-rata refund of prepaid charges; notice is "one month" effective at calendar month-end rather than 30 days), which the rationale correctly acknowledges rather than claims.
- The deterministic signal "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical false negative — the rendered Section 3.4 expressly grants Customer a convenience right; the substantive gap was only the uncapped early termination charges in 3.4(b), which the operation fixes.
- Minimality holds: the single insertion is ", capped at three (3) months' charges" in 3.4(b). No other words were deleted or paraphrased, the favourable one-month notice and the prerequisite-attachment structure are retained, and no extras (survival tails, refund mechanics, procedures) were added.
- Intent is preserved: the auto-renewal/non-renewal mechanic, breach termination, notice timing and the Attachment A / Service Option Attachment cross-references all survive; the cap qualifies an existing charge without creating an undefined term ('charges' is the contract's own fee vocabulary) or a dangling reference.
- If the team later wants the preferred position, the operative repairs are (i) replace "at least one month's prior written notice" and the "end of any calendar month" anchor with "thirty (30) (days') prior written notice", and (ii) add "IBM will refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis."

**Resubmitted: deviation (T4C), fallback target — validated (ok:true) and accepted.**

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",

]

**Resubmitted: deviation (T4C), preferred level — validated (ok:true) and accepted.**

The only change from the last submission targets the residual deterministic signal the verifier identified as a regex adjacency artifact: in §3.4 the grant words "Customer may terminate" and "for convenience" were separated by roughly forty words of parenthetical carve-out. Operation 1 now moves "for convenience" directly after "Customer may terminate" in the same sentence I was already editing to delete the month-end anchor — every other word of that sentence, including the prerequisite-Attachment carve-out, is retained verbatim, and the net word count is lower than the original.

Final package (all within §3.4):
1. **p0044** — "Customer may terminate for convenience this Agreement … or any Service Option Attachment …", with "at the end of any calendar month" deleted so our exit is not deferred to a month-end.
2. **p0045** — notice changed from "one month's" to "thirty (30) days'".
3. **After p0047** — one sentence: IBM refunds prepaid charges pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.

Element 4 (no Vendor mid-term convenience right) stays already met by §3.2's end-of-term, 90-day non-renewal mechanic, with §3.3 confined to cause. Subparagraph b, IBM's continuing-performance duty, and §3.5's accrued-charge acceleration are untouched; the uncapped Attachment A early-termination charges are flagged in the rationale as our fallback fallback-back position, not drafted, since no preferred element calls for a cap.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"preferred","mappings":[{"element":"Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[2]},{"element":"Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[3]},{"element":"Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.","status":"already_met","quote":"unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment."}]}

Finding rationale:
Section 3.4 lets us terminate for convenience, but only effective "at the end of any calendar month" on one month's notice, and nothing in Section 3.4 or 3.5 refunds prepaid charges - Section 3.5 only accelerates our accrued payment obligations. We target the preferred position: operation 1 states the convenience right expressly ("Customer may terminate for convenience") and removes the calendar month-end effectiveness anchor that would otherwise defeat a 30-day exit, operation 2 sets our notice at thirty (30) days, and operation 3 adds IBM's pro-rata refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period. No Vendor-side change is needed: IBM has no mid-term convenience right, its only exits being material breach (3.3) and end-of-term non-renewal on ninety (90) days' notice (3.2). We note but do not press a three-month cap on the Attachment A early termination charges, which is a fallback point we can revert to.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0045: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
p0047: In the event that Customer exercises its rights under this Section 3.4, IBM shall continue to fulfill all of its duties and obligations following the notice date and until the final termination date.
p0040: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered operative language:
Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.
Customer may terminate for convenience this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) by:
a. providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to IBM; and
In the event that Customer exercises its rights under this Section 3.4, IBM shall continue to fulfill all of its duties and obligations following the notice date and until the final termination date.
IBM will refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] We have taken our preferred position on convenience termination: we may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' prior written notice without waiting for a calendar month-end, and IBM refunds prepaid charges pro rata for the period after termination. We can discuss longer notice as a fallback if IBM needs it.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 3.4: "Customer may terminate for convenience this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ..." The Agreement is defined to include the Order Forms and Service Option Attachments, so the Agreement-level and attachment-level convenience right covers the element; the retained prerequisite-attachment carve-out is pre-existing language, not a new restriction.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Sub-clause a. now reads "providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to IBM", and the original "at the end of any calendar month" effectiveness anchor was deleted so termination takes effect on the 30-day notice rather than being pushed to a month-end.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "IBM will refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis." This is an express pro-rata basis (not merely a post-termination-period refund) and is tied to the Section 3.4 convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only exits in the cited text are material breach (3.3) and the Section 3.2 auto-renewal notice, which is expressly effective only "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — natural-term non-renewal assessed under RENEWAL, not mid-term T4C. No mid-term Vendor convenience right appears, so the element is met as already-satisfied without any edit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered notice is "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice", which is below the 60–90 day fallback band. (This is Customer-favourable and consistent with the preferred level being targeted.)

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No cap is inserted anywhere in the operative text; the drafter concedes the Attachment A early termination charges remain uncapped ("We note but do not press a three-month cap"). A comment note is not operative language. The retained "; and" after sub-clause a. also signals an un-edited sub-clause b. (termination charges) that is left uncapped.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not bite: Vendor holds no convenience right at all. Its only unilateral exit is the Section 3.2 non-renewal notice whose effect is expressly tied to "the end of the then-current term", so nothing permits a mid-term Vendor convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply because Vendor has no convenience right; in any event the only Vendor-side exit notice requires "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term".

reasons: All four preferred elements are met in operative language: an express "Customer may terminate for convenience" right over the Agreement and any Service Option Attachment, a thirty (30) day notice with the month-end effectiveness anchor removed, an express pro-rata refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period, and no Vendor mid-term convenience right (Section 3.2 is natural-term non-renewal, scored under RENEWAL).

The fallback level is incomplete (30-day notice sits outside the 60–90 day band and no three-month cap on early-termination charges is inserted), but position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, so this does not defeat the redline.

Minimality holds: three narrow operations (insert the convenience label, change one month to thirty (30) days, add the refund sentence). Deleting "at the end of any calendar month" is necessary to deliver the 30-day exit required by element 2, not a cosmetic cut. The prerequisite-attachment carve-out, the Section 3.4 continued-performance sentence, and Section 3.2 are all retained verbatim; no survival tail, expense language, or extra procedure was added.

Intent is preserved: Section 3.5's acceleration of accrued payment obligations is untouched and does not contradict a refund of unearned prepaid charges; no defined term, cross-reference, or commercial mechanic is left dangling by the edits.

Drafting caution (not a defect in the checked elements): the retained "; and" at the end of sub-clause a. indicates an un-rendered sub-clause b. If that sub-clause imposes Attachment A early termination charges, confirm it does not read as a penalty that offsets the new pro-rata refund; if it does, either cap it at three months' fees or state that the refund applies notwithstanding any termination charge.

Document: 3.1 Term

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-3f6a4498","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.1 Indemnification by IBM","rationale":"Section 8.1 sits at our fallback position and is therefore acceptable without redline. IBM expressly defends and indemnifies Bluefly and its Enterprise against third-party claims that IBM-provided Materials or Base Components (i.e. the deliverables and hosted components used to perform the Services) infringe patent, trademark, copyright or trade secret rights, and pays awarded damages, costs and reasonable attorneys' fees. The exclusions are the usual ones permitted at fallback — Customer-provided items incorporated into the Materials (p0092), Customer modifications (p0093), and combination/use with non-IBM products, data or apparatus (p0095) — and the remedy ladder is the customary procure-continued-use / modify / replace with functionally equivalent items, followed by a refund credit of amounts paid for the affected Materials or Base Components (p0091). On the super-cap element, the bargain is better than fallback: Section 9.1(a) carves indemnification payments under Section 8.1 out of IBM's $100,000 / twelve-month damages cap entirely, so the IP indemnity is uncapped rather than limited to 3x annual fees. Standard procedure (prompt written notice, IBM control, Customer cooperation with reimbursement of cooperation costs) is present. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM Services Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of IBM Base Terms — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Base Terms against our playbook and verified 19 findings. Seven positions are already acceptable and require no redline: IBM's IP indemnity (§ 8.1) sits at our fallback and is in fact better than fallback on the cap (indemnity payments are carved out of the $100,000 / twelve-month cap by § 9.1(a)), and we carry no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicitation burden (§ 14.16 Freedom of Action is helpful to us here).

The substantive work sits in three clusters:

- **Two critical/high IP and licence gaps.** Type II Materials default to IBM ownership with a licence back that is neither perpetual, royalty-free, modifiable, sublicensable nor scoped to our business, and § 14.18 lets IBM exploit our contact information for its own marketing and disclose it onward (§ 5.4 / § 7 / § 14.18). Separately, the Base Components licence runs to Bluefly, Inc. alone with no Affiliate coverage (§ 12.1).
- **Two walk-away items.** IBM has **no insurance obligation of any kind** despite hosting our environment and processing personal data, and IBM's investigation right in § 11.3 is unlimited in frequency, requires no notice and allocates no cost.
- **A cluster of exit, remedy and liability shortfalls.** No transition assistance, data return or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement (§ 3.5); no warranty period or remedy, with all Materials "AS IS" (§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c)); convenience termination limited to calendar month-end with no refund of prepaid charges and uncapped early termination charges (§ 3.4); no carve-outs from the mutual liability caps for confidentiality, gross negligence or willful misconduct, made worse by § 6's precedence over the confidentiality agreement; one-way assignment favouring IBM (§ 14.10); and New York law with no forum specified at all (§ 14.3).

One finding (**RENEWAL, § 3.2**) failed verification and is marked needs review before we send comments.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (fallback) | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | Uncapped IP indemnity via § 9.1(a) carve-out; no redline. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (with § 7, § 14.18) | Type II licence back not perpetual/royalty-free/modifiable/sublicensable; IBM markets our contact data. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No sourcing restriction on us. |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 12.1 License | Grant runs to Bluefly, Inc. only; no Affiliate mechanism. |
| 5 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No field-of-use or competing-product restriction. |
| 6 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.10 Assignment | One-way: IBM may assign freely, including to a competitor. |
| 7 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | Unlimited frequency, no notice, no cost allocation. |
| 8 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 14.3 Choice of Law | NY law is preferred, but no forum specified anywhere. |
| 9 | Medium | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Early termination charges set outside the Agreement and uncapped. |
| 10 | Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | No confidentiality / gross negligence / willful misconduct carve-outs; § 6 caps confidentiality breach. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No MFN burden on us. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant (preferred) | § 4.1 Charges | Charges tied to Services ordered; confirm Order Forms/SOAs. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.8 Personnel | No no-hire covenant. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal notice window | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 3.2 Renewal | 90-day non-renewal window exceeds our 60-day ceiling; re-verify before sending. |
| 15 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Month-end anchor only; no refund of prepaid charges. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | No transition, return, export or deletion obligation. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | No conformance warranty, no period, no remedy; § 5.4(c) "AS IS". |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing (walk-away)** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance obligation for a hosting provider handling personal data. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These two must be resolved; we should not sign as drafted.

1. **Vendor insurance — absent entirely (§ 14.12 / miscellaneous).** IBM hosts our environment and, per § 14.18, processes personal information on our behalf, yet carries no contractual coverage obligation. We are inserting a short clause at the preferred level: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M where IBM handles data belonging to, supplied by or processed for us, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request. Fallback available: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
2. **Unbounded investigation right (§ 11.3).** IBM may investigate suspected AUP violations with no frequency limit, no advance notice (the notice paragraph applies only before IBM restricts access or removes Content, and is excused in an emergency) and no cost allocation. We propose the fallback cure only: one investigation per year, 15 days' notice, IBM bears cost unless an underpayment exceeding 10% is found.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-verify RENEWAL (§ 3.2)** before comments go out — the finding failed verification. Substantively we expect to substitute sixty (60) days for ninety (90) days, retaining the mutual notice right, writing requirement, per-Attachment structure and term-end anchor. Renewal carries no uplift, so the price-cap point is not engaged; if any Service Option Attachment term exceeds 12 months we escalate to cap the renewal term at 12 months.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the deviations and gaps above, each at the level noted: IP (licence attributes plus business-purpose scope; confine IBM's use of our contact information to providing the Services); LICENSE (extend § 12.1 to Affiliates on written notice); ASSIGN (mutual successor right on notice, other assignments on consent not unreasonably withheld); GOVLAW (add exclusive New York County forum, leaving the choice-of-law sentence verbatim); LD (cap early termination charges at three months' charges and make them our sole liquidated amount); LOL-CAP (one mutual carve-out sentence in §§ 9.1(c) and 9.2(c)); T4C (express convenience right, 30 days' notice, remove the month-end anchor, pro-rata refund of prepaid charges); TRANSITION (insert transition assistance, Content return and certified deletion into § 3.5, which survives under § 14.2); WARRANTY (90-day software conformance, 30-day Services warranty, repair/replace/re-perform and refund, plus a carve-out from the § 5.4(c) AS IS disclaimer).
3. **Diligence on documents not before us:** confirm Attachment A, the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms contain no minimum volumes, minimum monthly charges or early termination amounts inconsistent with the LD and MINCOMMIT positions, and confirm no Attachment term exceeds 12 months.
4. **Note for the business, not redlined:** the broad Type I Materials licence back to IBM; the absence of an IBM-granted MFN in our favour; and, under INDEMN, the twelve-month refund-credit cap, the strict prompt-notice condition, and the breadth of our § 8.2(a)(3) indemnity for Services Recipient claims (partly mitigated by the § 8.2(c) carve-back for IBM's fault). We can raise any of these commercially if the negotiation allows."}
